text:
alex: Heads up — Kibana queries for trace_id correlation are returning partial IDs in eu-west1 and full IDs in us-west. Query cost spiked this morning.
shreya: saw that, alerts flagged Prometheus query latency > 5s around 09:12. SLO dashboards show increased log search cost.
alex: reproduced. Example Kibana filter I ran:
```
trace_id: "6f1a2b3c"
"request_id": "req_..."
```
mel: are logs truncated at ingestion? Loki ingest pipeline might be truncating fields.
ops-bot: [Alert] grafana/alert/slow_log_search fired: query_latency_p95 > 5s (duration: 3m)
jon: can you paste the Loki query you used?
alex: here's the Loki query I ran (shortened):
```
{job="redwood-logs"} |= "trace_id" | json | trace_id
|~ "6f1a"
```
shreya: note: we recently switched to line_length_limit=256 on loki-ingester config in eu-west1.
alex: aha — that would truncate long json fields (trace_id+kv cache), causing inconsistent matching across regions.
tim: changing line_length_limit requires rolling ingesters and will spike S3 writes if we reindex — cost tradeoff.
mel: possible quick fix: switch Kibana query to use request_id instead of trace_id where available. request_id is shorter and not truncated.
alex: agreed. Also reduce kibana time window and use `| logfmt` to avoid full json parsing — cuts query cost.
shreya: I'll open a runbook and schedule a controlled ingester roll with new limit 2048 for eu-west1. will propose canary on a single tenant.
jon: add temporary alert tweak: delay grafana slow_log_search to 2m to reduce noise while we roll.
ops-bot: @shreya created issue INF-4321: increase-loki-line-limit-eu-west1
alex: thanks. also adding a saved Kibana view that maps trace_id->request_id to aid troubleshooting.
mel: cost note: if we increase line limit across regions expect ~7-12% increase in storage for first 30d. flagging finance.
tim: cc @finance for temporary budget bump if needed.
shreya: rolling canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC. will post update.
alex: great. quick PR to Kibana saved objects will land in 10m.
mel: :thumbsup: 
jon: moving to resolve for now, will reopen if we see more truncation.
